newsitem.title: UK: Europe hotel occupancy up, takeovers likely - survey.
newsitem.headline: Europe hotel occupancy up, takeovers likely - survey.

text.p: Continued high occupancy levels and average room rates for hotels across Europe will cause a flurry of joint ventures, mergers and acquisitions as international hotel chains vie for dominance, a survey by consultants Arthur Andersen showed.

"As occupancy and average room rates recover from recession, hotel operators will seek opportunities to extend their distribution into their source markets, to strengthen brand recognition and reduce over-head costs," said Alex Kyriakidis, worldwide head of the group's hospitality and leisure services, in a statement.

According to the survey occupancy levels for Europe as a whole grew by nearly 2 percent in 1996 to 72.2 percent and average room rates rose by almost 7 percent. "Conditions are likely to improve further in 1997 as the European economy picks up, and average room rates will increase to make up some of the ground lost during the recession," said the Arthur Anderson survey.

London, Edinburgh and Manchester are among the top ten cities in Europe for the best performing hotels in terms of occupancy and room rates. London hotels outperformed all the other major cities in Europe in 1996 with an average room occupancy rate of 84.3 percent, said the survey.
Average room rates grew more than triple the rate of inflation at 9.7 percent in the English hotels surveyed to an average 62.48 stg.
